note: Both sets cover essentially the same 25 claims from the wiring schedule and all values are correctly bound to the right symbol rows (151, 150, 50, 34, 33, 32, 31, 20, 10) as shown in the table image. Set A names the properties precisely (e.g. 'conductor material', 'conductor configuration'), whereas Set B states two row-150 claims with the vague attributes 'material' and 'conductor'. Neither set invents values and neither misreads a size, so the only substantive difference is attribute precision, which favors A. Both sets leave out several schedule facts (row 150's #4G ground and 2-1/2" conduit, row 20's #12G ground, row 33's 6#10, row 50's 3#6, row 10's #12/2WG).
remarks: The text layer is badly scrambled (row labels detached from their descriptions, e.g. '150' paired with the 20-row conductor string); the table image is the reliable source and both extractions follow it correctly. Both sets share the slightly odd attribute 'ground conductor configuration' for what is really a ground conductor size (#8G) on row 50. Important facts both sets miss: row 150 ground #4G and 2-1/2" conduit, row 20 ground #12G, row 33 conductors 6#10, row 50 conductors 3#6, row 10 cable #12/2WG, plus the panel notes (150A/2P main breaker, main bonding jumper, 200A/2P NFDS NEMA 3R) and the organizer interface wiring (4 AWG copper to gnd; L1, L2 & N, no gnd). The two sets are near-duplicates, differing only in ordering and attribute wording.
